title: Intrinsic and extrinsic sizing
learningObjectives: Explain intrinsic and extrinsic sizing and use selectors or sizing rules appropriately.

understand.concept: Intrinsic sizing derives size from an element's content, such as min-content or max-content contributions. Extrinsic sizing uses constraints from the containing layout, such as an assigned width or available space. Real layout often combines both.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding intrinsic and extrinsic sizing helps explain why a grid or flex item may refuse to shrink, or why a long word changes a track size. Content and container constraints work together.
understand.analogy: Intrinsic size is what the content asks for; extrinsic size is what the surrounding layout offers.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the idea; selector matching and sizing follow CSS specifications and browser layout algorithms.

explain.narrative: The layout combines flexible track sizing with content-based contributions. Try removing minmax(0,1fr) and compare the effect of a long string.

questions.prompt: What does intrinsic sizing primarily consider?
questions.explanation: Intrinsic sizing uses the size contributions of the content and its formatting context.
